o1.biggest_strength: Every email serves one of the two habits that predict retention. It uses only the five allowed triggers, with skip rules and a day-8 branch that pushes each user to whichever habit they're missing, which goes straight at the 8% to 67% gap.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 sets a day-14 goal but compares it to a week-one 8% baseline. The holdout gets no onboarding email at all, so the series is never measured against the old series.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use one measurement window for the 8% baseline and goal. Add a second holdout on the old series so the win is measured against what we run today, not against silence.

o2.biggest_strength: The welcome, recurring-task, platform-branched device email and calm check-in are all very good. The drop list ties the projects email to the persona's 'perfect on Sunday, gone by Wednesday' trap.
o2.biggest_mistake: It spends the fifth email on a Pro upsell instead of finishing the habit work, so users who have one habit are never pushed to the second, the step worth 67% retention.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the Pro email with a day-8 'missing habit' email. Move Pro past day 30. Check that set-time reminders really are Pro-only before promising it.

reason: Both are calm, on-brand and use the triggers correctly, but Output 1 commits all five emails to the two habits that keep users. Output 2 spends its last email selling Pro and leaves the 'do both' gap open.
